title: Rav Zevid (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as Rava’s student who always spoke in Rava’s name, as in Shabbat 93a; Rosh Hashanah 6a; Sukkah 44a; Bava Kamma 5a, 21b, 27b, 28a, 33a and 65a; Bava Metzia 23a; Bava Batra 99b; and Horayot 11a. In Berakhot 25b: “Rav Zevid teaches it thus: Abaye said it is forbidden, and Rava said it is permitted”; and in Berakhot 58a: “Rava said — and some say Rav Zevid.”

He was likewise Abaye’s student, as in Sotah 32b, where he raised a difficulty against Abaye; in Avodah Zarah 38b, “Rav Zevid said: Thus said Abaye”; in Berakhot 46b he spoke in Abaye’s name; and in Shabbat 154a, “Rav Zevid teaches it thus: Rami bar Chama said,” etc.

All the great students of Abaye and Rava were his colleagues: Rav Papa, as in Gittin 89b, where Rav Papa raised an objection to him; in Zevachim 20b Rav Zevid raised a difficulty against Rav Papa; and in Berakhot 45b they are mentioned together.

Rav Mari (II) was his colleague, as in Chullin 117a, where he raised a difficulty against Rav Zevid, who said to him, “Concerning you the verse says,” etc.; and their words serve to explain Abaye’s words. Ameimar was like a student-colleague of his, as in Beitzah 22a, where Ameimar said to Rav Ashi: “There is Rav Zevid, who took the same position as you” (who raised a difficulty to me as you do — Rashi) “and I resolved it for him” (I answered it for him — Rashi); and in Chullin 76b Ameimar spoke in his name. This Rav Zevid taught the baraitot of Rabbi Oshaya, as in Bava Batra 95a and Avodah Zarah 55a, “Rav Zevid taught in [the baraita of] the school of Rabbi Oshaya,” and Rashi explains: in the baraita of Rabbi Oshaya’s school; and we likewise find the phrase in Bava Metzia 92a and Avodah Zarah 6b. In Yevamot 96a, “Rav Zevid taught, son of Rabbi Oshaya,” Hyman proposes reading “of the school of Rabbi Oshaya”; in Shevuot 47a and Avodah Zarah 33b, “Rav Zevid bar Oshaya taught,” Hyman proposes “of the school of Rabbi Oshaya,” and reports this reading in Dikdukei Soferim on Shevuot there, and so is the view of our master, the author of Seder HaDorot. Of his students we find Rav Kahana (Rav Ashi’s colleague), who raised difficulties against Rav Zevid, as in Bava Metzia 101a, Sotah 45a and Me’ilah 19a. According to the testimony of Rav Sherira Gaon in his Epistle, part 3, end of chapter 3, Rav Zevid headed the academy in Pumbedita from the year 688 to the year 696; for after Rava’s death the academies were divided: Rav Papa headed the academy in Naresh until 682, and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak in Pumbedita, and after him Rav Zevid. Of that time it is said in Kiddushin 72b that Rav Ashi said to Ameimar: “What is your view? … But in Rav Kahana’s school they do not teach so, and in Rav Papa’s school they do not teach so, and in Rav Zevid’s school they do not teach so.” Of his personal life we find in Bava Batra 151a that he married the mother of Rav Zutra bar Tuviah and divorced her. The cause of his death is related in Avodah Zarah 38b: Rabbi Chiyya Parva’ah came to the Exilarch’s house and ruled like Chizkiyah and Bar Kappara, who permit. Rav Zevid said to them: “Do not listen to him; thus said Abaye…” They gave him a cup of vinegar to drink, and he died.

notes.text: Years תרפח/תרצו/תרפב are 688/696/682 without an era conversion. The death account is abridged in Hyman; saved Davidson Avodah Zarah 38b paragraph6 explicitly has Abaye (אביי), while the supplied Hyman scalar has אביו. The English follows Abaye with this disclosure. Hyman’s Yevamot emendation is supplied as ברבי ר׳ אושעיא; the English renders the school interpretation required by his surrounding בדבי argument, without claiming that ברבי literally spells בדבי. His school emendations and academy chronology remain his proposals/account. בעסה״ד is read as בעל סדר הדורות. Reigned here concerns academy leadership.

The consulted Avodah Zarah 38b names Chiyya Parva’ah, Chizkiyah and Bar Kappara, then Rav Zevid’s warning in Abaye’s name and the vinegar followed by his death. It supports the disclosed Abaye reading beside Hyman’s supplied אביו. The direct episode does not independently establish Hyman’s academy chronology, his identification with other Zevid passages, or the school-of-Oshaya emendations. His always assertion, student-colleague argument and dates 688, 696 and 682 remain his account without an era conversion; the supplied ברבי and his contextual בדבי interpretation remain distinct.
